headline: Apple Maps India Now Says 'Turn Right After the Petrol Pump'

image.licence: Apple Newsroom press image (official), credited 'Image: Apple'
image.author: Apple
image.subject: iPhone 18 Pro showing an Apple Maps Look Around street-level view of the Qutb Minar and Alai Darwaza, Qutb Complex, New Delhi (Apple's caption: 'A Maps screen on iPhone 18 Pro shows the Qutb Complex in New Delhi')

framing.note: pipeline.framing ok (full-bleed, faces 0); cover zoomed to 1.3 so the screen fills the frame and the Minar top clears the logo; a few distant visitors at the monument's base are specks, not identifiable

fact_sources.fact: Apple rolled out an all-new Apple Maps for India on 18 Nov 2026, available from today ('today's rollout')
Look Around street-level imagery now in India (examples: BMC building, Mumbai; Qutb Complex, New Delhi)
Natural Language Guidance uses real-world details on unnamed roads, e.g. 'Turn right after the petrol pump'
Dual-language labels, based on the device language and the region's local language: on a device set to English, Hindi + English around Delhi, Marathi + English around Mumbai

Maps supports English and Hindi and has added Bengali, Gujarati, Kannada, Malayalam, Marathi, Tamil, Telugu, Punjabi, Odia and Urdu (Apple's list: 10 added; Business Standard says 11, Gizbot implies 12 total; we count Apple's own list)
Dual-language labels and enhanced Natural Language Guidance need iOS 27.2 (iPadOS/watchOS/macOS 27.2) or later
Transit in Ahmedabad, Bengaluru, Chennai, Delhi, Hyderabad, Kolkata, Mumbai and Pune plus Indian Railways; find nearby stations, pin favourite routes, alert when it's time to get off
AR walking directions; lane guidance before turns and elevated roads; multi-stop routes of up to 15 stops

tag_evidence: No tag: apple.com (/in/, global home page and the newsroom article) has no link to an Instagram account, so the @apple handle can't be confirmed from Apple's own site as required.
